extracted.intended_audience: individual investors and members of the public who want to submit comments on SEC rulemaking/releases
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content guidance for members of the public (especially individual investors) who wish to submit comment letters on SEC Proposed Rules, Concept Releases, SRO filings, PCAOB rulemaking, petitions, and other releases. Describes acceptable submission methods, formatting and labeling requirements, and publication/redaction policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments will be made available to the public. Comments sent via online form or e-mail will be posted on the SEC website. Comments sent via paper will be converted to PDF and then posted on the SEC website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware your submission becomes public when you submit it. Paper submissions will be digitized (PDF) prior to posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid submitting personally identifiable information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; submit only information that you wish to make available publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think carefully before including names, addresses, Social Security numbers, or other PII because the SEC will post comments publicly and may not fully redact such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC redaction/withholding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit material you do not want published; obscene material or copyrighted material may be redacted or withheld by the SEC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only one submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: To help the SEC process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a single submission channel (online form, e-mail, or paper) for your comment; do not send the same comment through multiple channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the SEC internet comment form when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you find the rule or release you want to comment on from one of the relevant index pages, you can access the online comment form through a 'Submit a Comment' or similar link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may need to click to the rule or release page before seeing the link to the comment form. You can include attachments to the form. Note: Comments on Rulemaking Petitions cannot be submitted by online form.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail submission address and subject-line requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Send comments to rule-comments@sec.gov. The subject line of your message must include the File Number for the rule, release, or petition. This is the number that begins 'S7-', 'SR-', 'PCAOB-', or '4-'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including the correct File Number in the subject line ensures the SEC associates your comment with the proper rule/release/petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted attachment formats and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC accepts comment letters in PDF format. If you attach a document, indicate the format or software used (e.g., PDF, Word Perfect, MS Word, ASCII text, etc.). DO NOT submit attachments as HTML, GIF, TIFF, PIF, ZIP, or EXE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer PDF for attachments. If using other common formats, state which software/format you used. Avoid executable or uncommon image/archive formats listed as disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper comment letter mailing address and referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Address your letter to: Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090. All submissions should refer to the 'File Number' for the rule, release, or petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper submissions will be converted to PDF and posted. Always include the File Number (e.g., 'S7-', 'SR-', 'PCAOB-', '4-') in paper comments so they are associated correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special procedure for Rulemaking Petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments on Rulemaking Petitions cannot be submitted by online form and must be submitted by e-mail or on paper (see the instructions for these two methods below). If you submit a comment on a Rulemaking Petition, be sure to include the associated file number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to use the online comment form for petitions; follow the e-mail or paper instructions and ensure the file number is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of duplicate or near-identical comments
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple comments are submitted with identical or near-identical content, only the first copy of the comment received will be posted publicly, along with a running total number of that comment received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If organizing a mass-submission campaign, note that only the first will be posted in full; subsequent identical submissions will be tallied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding via Feedback Flyer (when available)
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally, a link to a 'Feedback Flyer' will be made available for a proposal. Feedback Flyers are designed specifically for individual investor comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback Flyers can be submitted by a specialized webform, e-mail (scanned and provided as an attachment), or via postal mail in hard copy; they contain questions relevant to individual investors and are an alternative submission mechanism when provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locate open rules/releases via SEC index pages
rubrics_metrics.description: To locate rules or releases open for comment, browse the relevant index pages: Proposed Rules; Concept Releases; Self-Regulatory Organization (SRO) filings; Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) Rulemaking; Rulemaking Petitions; Other Releases; Interpretive Releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding the correct index page helps you identify the File Number and link to the appropriate 'Submit a Comment' form or instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate file number on all submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should refer to the 'File Number' for the rule, release, or petition. This is the number that begins 'S7-', 'SR-', 'PCAOB-', or '4-'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated emphasis: include the correct file number in the body or subject of your submission so SEC staff can correctly process and associate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to additional guidance for individual investors
rubrics_metrics.description: For more on the SEC rulemaking process and suggestions on how to write your comment, see 'Suggestions for How Individual Investors Can Comment on SEC Rulemaking: Updated Investor Bulletin.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The referenced bulletin provides further tips on content and approach tailored to individual investors who wish to submit effective comments.
